proofs.full_local_argument: This is a proposed local argument, not a quotation or an independently accepted proof. Fix one CndG call with β>0, η>0 and diameter D>0. Write φ(x)=<g,x>+β||x-u||²/2, C=βD², φ*=min_X φ, δ_t=φ(u_t)-φ*, and G_t=<∇φ(u_t),u_t-v_t>, where v_t is any exact LO minimizer. Compactness gives all minima. Convexity and the LO property imply 0≤δ_t≤G_t. If the algorithm has not terminated at test t, then G_t>η>0, hence v_t≠u_t; the denominator in (2.5) is positive and (2.5) minimizes φ on the segment. For every trial a∈[0,1], the quadratic identity and ||v_t-u_t||≤D therefore give δ_{t+1}≤δ_t-aG_t+Ca²/2≤(1-a)δ_t+Ca²/2. This holds for every performed update. If the algorithm stops earlier than any index used below, the desired upper budget already holds. Otherwise, at t=1 choose a=1 to obtain δ_2≤C/2, independently of δ_1; no bound on arbitrary initial error is assumed. We claim δ_t≤2C/t for all reached t≥2. The base follows from δ_2≤C/2≤C. Given the claim at t, choose a=2/(t+1), which belongs to [0,1]. Then δ_{t+1}≤2C(t-1)/[t(t+1)]+2C/(t+1)²≤2C/(t+1), since the difference between the last upper bound and the preceding expression is 2C/[t(t+1)²]>0. This proves the induction. Now fix an integer m≥2 and suppose all tests j=m,...,2m-1 fail. Their updates are performed. For each such update use the trial a=1/m in the stronger inequality δ_{j+1}≤δ_j-G_j/m+C/(2m²). Rearrangement and summation yield (1/m)Σ_{j=m}^{2m-1}G_j≤δ_m-δ_{2m}+C/(2m)≤2C/m+C/(2m)=5C/(2m), because δ_{2m}≥0. In the selected outer iteration k≥1, C=β_kD_X² and C/η_k=3k. Choose m=9k≥2. The resulting average gap is at most 5η_k/6<η_k, contradicting the assumption that every gap in that block exceeds η_k. Therefore some test with index at most 2m-1=18k-1 succeeds. Exactly one LO query is made per test, starting at index 1; a successful test performs no update. Thus this call makes at most 18k-1 LO calls, including its final successful test, and at most 18k-2 updates. Summing over k=1,...,N gives at most Σ(18k-1)=9N²+8N LO calls. Each outer iteration queries f' once, and inner quadratic gradients use the saved g, so exactly N gradient queries are charged. At a successful test, the LO definition implies <∇φ(x_k),x_k-x>≤η_k for every x∈X, namely the certificate (2.8). Consequently the finite outputs satisfy the conditions required by the source outer-error proof Theorem 2(a). Substituting γ_k=3/(k+2), β_k=3L/(k+1), η_k=LD_X²/[k(k+1)] gives Γ_k=6/[k(k+1)(k+2)], β_kγ_k/Γ_k=3Lk/2, Lγ_k≤β_k, and γ_1=1. In (2.15), the diameter term equals 9LD_X²/[2(k+1)(k+2)], while η_iγ_i/Γ_i=LD_X²/2 for each i, so the accumulated tolerance term is 3LD_X²/[(k+1)(k+2)]. Their sum is 15LD_X²/[2(k+1)(k+2)], the source conclusion. This last substitution uses the read source Theorem 2(a), without adopting Theorem 2(c). Choosing the integer N stated in the conclusion makes the displayed objective bound at most ε. The budgets are consequently O(1+sqrt(LD_X²/ε)) gradients and O(1+LD_X²/ε) LO calls for all ε>0, implying the source asymptotics as ε→0. No lower-bound or transfer claim is made.

assumptions: L>0 and D_X>0; singleton and zero-L degeneracies are excluded from this implementation.
For every integer k≥1 use β_k=3L/(k+1), γ_k=3/(k+2), η_k=LD_X²/[k(k+1)].
Each CndG call uses exact segment minimization (2.5) and terminates only after its exact Wolfe gap is at most η_k.
statement.conclusion: Source Corollary 3 states f(y_k)-f(x*)≤15LD_X²/[2(k+1)(k+2)] for all k≥1, with FO complexity O(sqrt(LD_X²/ε)) and LO complexity O(LD_X²/ε). Its proof reports 9N²+10N inner iterations. Separately, the proposed local repair below derives at most 18k-1 actual LO calls in outer iteration k, including the terminal test, hence at most 9N²+8N LO calls and exactly N gradient queries through outer iteration N. This local numerical budget is not attributed to the authors and is submitted for new independent review, with no acceptance of this new hash claimed. A sufficient integer limit is N=max{1,ceil(sqrt(15LD_X²/(2ε)))}; thus the all-ε budgets have additive constants, and the displayed source asymptotics concern ε→0 with L,D_X fixed.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let X⊆R^n be nonempty compact convex with an inner-product-induced norm, dual norm ||·||_*, and diameter D_X=max_{x,y∈X}||x-y||. Let f:X→R be convex differentiable, f*=min_X f, and x* any minimizer. Run Algorithm 1 from y_0=x_0∈X, using exact gradients and exact linear optimization as described in alg.P010.cgs.
statement.parameter_domains: n≥1 integer; L,D_X>0; outer limit N≥1 integer; ε>0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such instance, every feasible x_0, every optimal x*, every admissible choice among exact LO minimizers, and every integer k≥1. No prescribed randomization.
